accepted_claim: For a noncircular ellipse with a strictly nested nondegenerate confocal elliptical caustic and periodic billiard family, the ordinary one-focus vertex-distance product is independent of real phase if and only if the primitive least period n is congruent to 2 modulo 4. All admissible primitive star turns and both orientations are included. For every positive repeat count r the r-fold product is the r-th power of the primitive product, so constancy and nonconstancy are preserved exactly. A circle is a separate trivial constant case.
strongest_original_claim: The submitted primitive n=2 modulo4 theorem is mathematically valid and yields equal positive products for the two foci.
source_scope_issue: The source entry does not explicitly define least period. An unqualified return-length N=2 modulo4 assertion is false. The strengthened classification fully decides this interpretation; it must not be represented as making its unrestricted invariant true.
exact_counterexample: a²=15,b²=7,c²=8, alpha²=135/16,beta²=7/16; primitive triangle ((a,0),(-3a/4,±7/4)) and its central reflection have ordinary focal products 15a/2±3c. Their doubled six-event products differ by180√30.
proof_mechanisms: Published canonical real parametrization independently checked by Jacobi chord tangency, reflection and full real-phase coverage.
Full Jacobi-sine torus has two simple pole classes and two simple zeros for each ordinary focal factor; complete divisors are verified.
The two zeros differ by one billiard step. Their common subgroup coset cancels the pole coset precisely when n=2 modulo4; other least periods retain poles.
Compact-torus holomorphy proves constancy; identity theorem transfers uncancelled complex poles to real physical-family nonconstancy.
Strict positivity makes integer powers injective and proves the exact repetition classification.
numerical_evidence_limit: Diagnostics use ordinary high-precision or floating-point computations; neither finite sampling nor unvalidated numerical error estimates prove the universal theorem. The analytic proof and exact controls do.
